B_acceptedByNormalizer.title: The new pagination tests cover only the listing, while the existing CSV tests never send a valid non-default limit or offset. A regression that accidentally paginates the export would therefore pass: all six seed records fit in the default page. Add an export assertion with a small limit and nonzero offset that still expects the whole filtered set.

This new helper returns any, so TypeScript cannot check the response properties used throughout these tests. Return a typed payload (or unknown with validation) instead, so incorrect field names and types are caught by type checking.

The new listing rejection tests do not exercise an invalid offset, although /records promises a 400 with the offending field. The existing invalid-offset test only calls /records.csv, so a listing-specific regression in query handling could pass. Add /records cases for a negative or non-integer offset and an offset above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
